chatra_classical_rule.formation_text: The seven planets in seven consecutive houses from the 7th (7-1) (parasol).

ardhachandra_classical_rule.formation_text: The seven planets in seven consecutive houses beginning from a non-kendra (half-moon).

kedara_classical_rule.formation_text: The seven planets occupy four signs (field).

analysis: Chatra/Ardhachandra both classically require the 7 classical planets to occupy 7 DISTINCT consecutive houses (one planet per house in the window) -- fundamentally different from Kedara's '4 distinct signs occupied' count rule. The native chart's 7 planets occupy only 4 distinct houses (7,9,10,11), satisfying Kedara but categorically failing Chatra/Ardhachandra's spread requirement, yet the system fires all three.
